blocking_findings.detail: Apache Commons IO XmlStreamReader uncontrolled resource consumption (DoS). Grype/GHSA rates this HIGH (CVSS 7.5) with fix 2.14.0 available. Not touched by this PR (still pinned at 2.4). NVD-sourced Stage 1 report scored the same CVE MEDIUM (4.3) using a different CVSS vector variant (UI:R vs UI:N) -- Grype/GHSA is the authoritative source for this check per skill policy.

Denied/flagged license under project policy. Pre-existing on main (was already GPL-2.0 at 8.0.30); the version bump to 8.0.33 in this PR resolves CVE-2023-22102 for the CVE check but does not change the license, which the PR body itself calls out as an open policy decision. Per audit skill Step 6, a denied/violation license is an unconditional BLOCK condition regardless of who introduced the dependency.

Non-allowlisted, plain-HTTP repository declared in pom.xml (pre-existing seeded 'ISSUE #5' content, unchanged by this PR). No artifact in the current resolved dependency tree actually resolves from it (dependency:tree confirms all artifacts resolve from Maven Central) -- flagged here as a standing repository-configuration risk per skill Step 4, not as a resolved-artifact provenance violation. Recommend removing the repository block entirely as a follow-up hardening action.

warnings.detail: GHSA advisory for the legacy 'mysql:mysql-connector-java' GAV lists the vulnerable range as <=8.0.33 with no fix recorded under that coordinate -- upstream's actual remediation requires migrating to the relocated 'com.mysql:mysql-connector-j' artifact id (Maven build already emits a relocation warning for this). Not a hard BLOCK line under skill policy (no available fix under the current coordinate), but should be tracked -- see tracking issue.
